paragraphs: Mikkelal hammelakot haregilot etzel haadam shebbenaqel epshar sheyyikkashel bahem utzerikin hashgacha beyoter, hu meleket haqqosher vehammattir, shehaadam ragil bazeh bime hachol harbeh, vehayyadayim asqaniyyot hem bedabar zeh tamid. vehinneh min haddin asur liqshor qesher shel qeyama; vekol qesher sheeno asuy lehattir bo bayyom chashib shel qayma, veasur midderabbanan "p shehu qesher hedyot veeno qesher umman. al ken, kol qesher sheeno asuy lehattir bo bayyom, yaasennu aniba achat velo qesher gamur. vekol qesher sheasur leqashero, asur lehattiro beshabbat.

clarification.explanation: The labor of tying and untying is especially easy to violate inadvertently, since the hands are always accustomed to it during the week. By strict law, it is forbidden to tie a "permanent knot"; and any knot not intended to be untied that same day is considered "permanent" and rabbinically forbidden, even if it is an ordinary knot (not a craftsman's knot). Therefore, a knot that will not be untied that same day — one should make only a bow, not a full knot. A forbidden knot — it is also forbidden to untie it.
takeaways: A knot not intended to be untied that same day is forbidden (even a simple knot); one should make only a bow instead.

paragraphs: Vekol qesher sheasuy lehattir bo bayyom muttar leqashero beshabbat. bammeh debarim amurim? qesher hedyot, abal qesher umman aseru. vekol sheoseh shene qesharim zeh al zeh, chashib keqesher umman veasur, "p sheasuy lehattir bo bayyom. veal-ken tzarik lehizzaher lebilti yiqshor hammiknasayim o hachagora asher bammiknasayim shene qesharim zeh al zeh, "p shehem asuyim lehattir bo bayyom, ella yaaseh qesher echad, vaaniba achat al gabbayv. veheerakti bedin shel shene qesharim zeh al zeh besipre haq' "rab-pealim", veheeleti lahalaka leesor. veda, mah shekkatab haggaon chida" za"l b"birke-yosep" vezeh leshono: velet dechash lah ella miuta demiuta debateli bemiutayhu - en kavvanato al happoseqim za"l, ella al anshe gelilotayv, deqae alayhu, dela chayeshi bezeh ella miuta demiuta debateli bemiutayhu, legabbe rubba deinashe deotam gelilot.

clarification.explanation: A knot intended to be untied that same day — is permitted to tie (if it is an ordinary knot, not a craftsman's knot). But two knots tied one over the other are considered a craftsman's knot — forbidden, even if it will be untied that same day. Therefore one must be careful not to tie trousers or a belt with two knots, but rather one knot with a bow over it.
takeaways: Two knots tied one over the other (even if untied that same day) are forbidden as a craftsman's knot; one should make one knot plus a bow.

paragraphs: Bimqom tzaar, katebu happoseqim za"l deen chush behattarat shene qesharim zeh al zeh, kegon sheshshakach veqashar hammiknasayim shene qesharim vehutzrak linqabayv, demuttar lehattiram, veken kayyotze bazeh bimqom tzaar.

clarification.explanation: In a case of distress (for example, one forgot and tied his trousers with two knots and urgently needs to relieve himself) — it is permitted to untie them, following the law of any case of distress.
takeaways: Untying forbidden double knots is permitted in a case of urgent distress (such as a physical need).

paragraphs: Im oseh qesher echad berosh hachut o chebel o meshicha, dino kemo shene qesharim zeh al zeh, dekol keha mitqayyem tepe vehave qesher chazaq apillu shehu qesher echad. veen qosherin deli bechebel im haddeli qabua babbor, dimbattel leh hatam vehave qesher shel qeyama; veim qosher bachagora vekayyotze, muttar, dela mebattel leh.

clarification.explanation: A single knot at the end of a thread or rope — is considered as strong as two knots (since it holds well), and therefore has the law of a permanent knot. One should not tie a bucket to a rope if the bucket is permanently fixed at the well (this makes it permanent there — a permanent knot); with a belt and the like — it is permitted (it does not make it permanent there).
takeaways: A single knot at the end of a thread that holds well is treated as a double knot (forbidden).

paragraphs: Hechaluq sheqqorin bearbi "qametz" (kuttonet), yesh tolin lah berasheha etzel hatztzavvar shene chutin kede leqasheran zeh al zeh, utzerikim lizzaher shel yeqashsherum ella raq yaasu aniba, yaan ki zeh haqqesher eno asuy lehattir bo bayyom; vaapillu im qosheram beereb shabbat mibbeod yom, gam ken lo yeqashsherem, shemma yitztarek lipshot hachilluq beshabbat veyitztarek lehattir, vekol qesher sheasur leqashero, asur lehattiro. veyoter tob shello yaasu lachaloq chutin al derek haamur, ella yaaseh sham lulaot sheqqorin bearbe "zarur" (lulaa chitzonit), veaz bazeh lo yabo lide mikshol.

clarification.explanation: The threads hanging at the neck of a shirt for tying — one should make only a bow, not a knot (since it will not be untied that same day). Even if tied before the Sabbath — one should not tie a knot, since one might need to remove the shirt on the Sabbath and untie a forbidden knot. It is preferable to sew loops instead of tying threads, in order to avoid the pitfall entirely.
takeaways: For garment-tying threads, it is preferable to use loops rather than threads requiring a knot, in order to avoid the pitfall entirely.

paragraphs: Happotel chabalim mikkol min sheyyihyeh, chayyab mishshum qosher; veshiuro, kede sheyyaamod hachebel biptilato belo qeshira, shennimtzet melakto mitqayyemet. veken hammaprid happetil, chayyab mishshum mattir im eno mitkavven leqalqel bilbad; veshiuro kehappotel.

clarification.explanation: Twisting ropes (of any kind) carries liability under tying, at the measure where the rope will hold together without additional tying (a lasting labor). One who separates a twisted strand (without intent to damage) is liable under untying, at the same measure.
takeaways: Twisting a rope and separating it carry liability under tying/untying, at the measure where the labor lasts.

paragraphs: Yesh sheoser lehachazir retzuot hammiknasayim vekaddomeh shennishmetu im hanneqeb tzar vetzarik torach. veken yesh mi sheomer - im hammiknasayim chadashim, asur lehaknis bahem haretzua im bedato lebattelah sham, dehave lah metaqqen mana.

clarification.explanation: Some forbid putting back a trouser drawstring that has slipped out if the opening is narrow and difficult. Likewise with new trousers, if one intends to leave the drawstring there permanently — this is considered "repairing a vessel" and is forbidden.
takeaways: Putting back a slipped trouser drawstring requires caution, especially if one intends to leave it there permanently.

paragraphs: Beged hattapur veomed, venitparedu shette chatikot habbeged zeh mizzeh bemiqtzat, asur limtoach rosh hachut lehaddeqo kede lechabberam, ki zo hi tepirato vechayyab mishshum toper.

clarification.explanation: A sewn garment, part of which has come apart — it is forbidden to pull the end of the thread to rejoin it (this is sewing, and one is liable under sewing).
takeaways: Rejoining parts of a garment that came apart by pulling a thread is forbidden (considered sewing).

paragraphs: Mah shemmechabberim hallebush "y machat - im tochabin oto shette techibot davqa muttar, veim shalosh techibot, asur. bammeh debarim amurim? beoseh ken al daat lehitqayyem ezeh yamim, kegon mah sheosim hammitznepet, veken bemalbushe hannashim, sheoseh zeh leqayyem ezeh yamim, abal mah sheosin lepi shaa, kegon lechabber tzidde hatztzaip o mekasseh happanim bitziatam chutz labbayit, muttar apillu beshalosh techibot, deen zeh ella leshaa, ki bevadday sheyyippashetu hatztzaip kesheyyachzeru lebetam; mihu, kevan deyesh machmirim beshalosh gam baenu asuy lehitqayyem, tob lehizzaher heka deepshar lahem bishte techibot; veayyen "ginnat-veradim", kelal g', siman y"z-y"ch, v"tl-orot" dap n"h.

clarification.explanation: Joining a garment with a needle: two stitches are permitted, three are forbidden — this applies specifically when one intends it to last several days (such as a permanent turban or women's garments). For a temporary joining (such as closing a scarf to go out, to be removed upon returning home) — even three stitches are permitted, though it is good to be careful with two when possible.
takeaways: Joining a garment with a needle for lasting use is limited to two stitches; for a purely temporary joining, even three are permitted.

paragraphs: Mokin shennapelu min hakkeset, muttar lehachaziram; abal asur letannam battechilla bakkeset, gezera shemma yitpor; veod, dimtaqqen mana hu, sheakshav osehu keli. vbsh"q "mqbtzl" katabti, deyesh lizzaher shello yannicha begadim betok hakkis kede sheyyihyeh kemo kar lishon alayv.

clarification.explanation: Stuffing (filling material) that fell out of a cushion — it is permitted to put it back; but it is forbidden to insert it for the first time into a cushion (concern that one might sew it, and also "repairing a vessel"). One should not place garments in a pillowcase to serve as a cushion for sleeping.
takeaways: Stuffing that fell out of a cushion may only be put back, not inserted for the first time.

paragraphs: En lenatteq o lachtok zug minalim hattepurim zeh im zeh apillu rotzeh lelabesham beshabbat; veyesh lehattir "y goy. umuttar lilbosh anpilaot chadashim, veen chosheshin shemma yenattequ chutin; veim nittaq o niqra, dabar sheeno mitkavven hu velav pesiq resheh veshari. veken potzein haegoz bematlit, veen chosheshin shemma tiqqara, delav pesiq resheh hu.

clarification.explanation: One should not separate a pair of shoes sewn together, even in order to wear them on the Sabbath (they should be separated by a gentile). It is permitted to wear new socks without concern that threads might tear; and if they tore inadvertently (unintentionally) — it is permitted. Cracking nuts with a cloth — there is no concern it will tear, since this is not certain (not an inevitable result).
takeaways: Sewn-together shoes should not be separated; but actions where tearing is not certain (wearing, cracking a nut) are permitted.

paragraphs: Hammedabbeq neyarot o orot beqolan shel soperim vekayyotze, hare zeh toledet toper; veken hampareq neyarot debuqim, hare zeh toledet qorea vechayyab. bammeh debarim amurim? kesheddibbuq zeh naasa leqiyyum, abal dappe separim shennidbequ zeh im zeh "y shaava o bishat haqqeshira, muttarim lepatechan beshabbat, kevan dela naasu leqiyyum; velo od, ella shennaasa zeh meelayv belo mitkavven, eno domeh letoper veen bo mishshum qorea.

clarification.explanation: Gluing papers or hides together permanently (with glue) is a derivative of sewing; separating them is a derivative of tearing and carries liability. But book pages that stuck together by mistake (wax at the time of binding, not for permanence) — it is permitted to separate them, since there was no intent of sewing.
takeaways: Gluing or separating something intended to be permanent is forbidden; pages stuck together by mistake (not intentionally permanent) may be separated.

paragraphs: Haggozez sear – ben min hachay, ben min hammet, ben min behema, ben min chayya, apillu meor hammupshat – chayyab min hattora. vehattolesh tzemer beyado mehabbehema o chayya, patur min hattora veasur middibre soperim. vehattolesh sear meor behema o chayya – ben im asao leoto or malbush kegon "parva", ben lo asao malbush – hare zeh chayyab min hattora, mippene ki telishat hassear zo hi gizzato, vela dame letzemer. veyesh omerim sheggam tolesh sear eno chayyab ella middibre soperim; laken haadam yasim dato bedabar zeh, ki yadayim asqaniyyot hen. gam lipamim yidbaq bapparva ezeh garin shel temara o shel abattichim vekayyotze, veim yasir haggarin, mukrach sheyyinnateq sheyyearot, vahare kan sepeq issur tora, vegam issur vadday middibre soperim.

clarification.explanation: Shearing hair (from any animal, living or dead, even from a flayed hide) is Torah-liable. Plucking wool by hand from a living domestic or wild animal is exempt from Torah liability but rabbinically forbidden. Plucking hair from a hide (such as fur) — according to the first opinion is Torah-liable, since plucking hair here is akin to shearing it; but some say that even one who plucks hair from a hide is forbidden only rabbinically, not by Torah law. Due to this dispute, one must be especially careful of seeds (of a date, watermelon, and the like) that stick to fur — removing them necessarily plucks out hairs, and so there is here a doubt of a Torah prohibition (according to the stricter view) alongside a certain rabbinic prohibition (according to all views).
takeaways: Shearing/plucking hair from an animal's hide is severe; one opinion holds it is Torah-liable, while others hold it is only rabbinically forbidden.
One must be especially careful of seeds stuck in fur — removing them may pluck out hair, carrying a doubt of a Torah prohibition alongside a certain rabbinic one.

paragraphs: Asur littol shiaru o tzipparenayv – ben bayyad, ben bikli, ben leatzmo, ben laacherim; veim natal shette sheyyearot bikli, chayyab chattat beshogeg useqila bemezid; ubesear echad, asur min hattora kedin chatzi shiur. ubannotel beyado, asur middibre soperim apillu sear echad. velaken yizzaher shello yechakkek harbeh bazzaqan velo yitasseq sham, shemma yitlosh sear. veken hannashim, sheyyesh lahem sheyyearot harbeh berosham, lo yachkeku harbeh betzippareniyyim shellahem, devadday yitleshu sheyyearot. ubetok hachotem shekicha sheyyearot, veyizzaher leqanneach tzoat hachotem sheyyabesha qetzat benachat, shello yaaqor sheyyearot. veken keshemmeqanneach baasiyyat tzerakayv, yizzaher leharbot bemayim, viqanneach beripyon yadayim, sheim yihyu mayim muatin viqanneach bechozeq, yittaleshu nimin bevadday.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to remove hair or fingernails (by hand or with an implement, for oneself or another). Removing two hairs with an implement is Torah-liable (stoning if deliberate); one hair is Torah-forbidden ("half the measure"); by hand — even one hair is rabbinically forbidden. One must be careful of scratching a beard, scratching the head with fingernails, cleaning the nose, and wiping after relieving oneself — all of these might inadvertently pluck out hair. And since hairs are commonly present inside the nostrils, one should be careful to gently wipe away dried mucus, so as not to uproot hairs.
takeaways: Removing hair or fingernails is forbidden in every form; one must be careful of everyday actions (scratching, wiping) that might inadvertently pluck out hair.

paragraphs: Hattolesh notza meopot vetarnegolim – ben chayyim, ben metim – chayyab, dearechah behaki vehave gozez.

clarification.explanation: Plucking a feather from a bird or chicken (living or dead) is Torah-liable, since this is a manner of shearing.
takeaways: Plucking feathers from a bird carries liability as shearing.

paragraphs: Asur litlosh qelippot basar mibbesaro; veikka disbira lehu sheyyesh bazeh issur tora. vetzipporen shepparesha rubbah umetzaeret oto, muttar littol beyado abal lo bikli. vetzitzin kemin retzuot daqqot sheppereshu meor haetzba sabib latztzipporen umetzaarot oto, muttar min haddin letallam bayyad; ak kevan deyesh pelugta ben rashi"y za"l verabbenu tam za"l bepareshu kelappe mala – im hu kelappe rashe etzbeotayv o keneged haggup – laken asur letallam apillu bayyad. vehaishsha shechal tebilatah belel-shabbat, veshakecha littol tzippareneha mibbeod yom – nahagnu poh irenu y" meabotenu lehorot kisbarat hashsha"k, lahasiram "y goya; veraq melammedin et haggoya shehi timshok yede haishsha kede laqutz, velo tiqrab haishsha et yadah eleha.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to peel skin flakes from the body (some hold this is a Torah prohibition). A fingernail that is mostly detached and causes distress — it is permitted to remove it by hand (not with an implement). Hangnails (strips of skin around the nail) — there is a dispute regarding the direction of separation, and therefore it is forbidden to remove them even by hand. A woman whose immersion falls on Sabbath night, who forgot to trim her fingernails beforehand — the custom in Baghdad was to permit this through a gentile woman (who pulls the woman's hand, without the woman herself drawing her hand close).
takeaways: Peeling skin or hangnails is forbidden (a mostly-detached fingernail — permitted by hand only); a woman who forgot to trim her nails before a Sabbath-night immersion has a solution through a gentile woman.
